items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: the group -- there was a guy by the name of Billy Milton, a guitarist, and little Lonnie Charles; he played guitar... And like I said, we went back hustling

ctx.x: Well, that's how I came up -- I didn't have a musical

education -- but I learned by listening and doing. And like I said, when I left the Tuxedo Inn, I went down to -- the club just folded up; that was about '30 -- I went back to hustling with a group. Now, the group -- there was a guy by the name of Billy Milton, a guitarist, and little Lonnie Charles; he played guitar, and he had another guy named Bill who sang -- singing 4-part harmony, we had a cat out in front mugging. and he had another cat.

And like I said, we went back hustling to all the big nightclubs way up north in Chicago, not on the south side, because there wasn't much money out there, but all up Broadway; I remember the 5100 Club; you'd see Danny Thomas in there. And Lord Buckley -- Dick Buckley. They had shows, but they would let us in to come do a spot, and people would throw out coins, money on the floor. We'd make it like that.
